title: SLA Credit & Incident Evidence Retention Playbook
author: Aisha Kumar
body:
Purpose

This playbook defines the evidence retention, collection, and SLA-credit determination workflow for incidents affecting Redwood Inference customer-facing SLOs. It is intended for on-call responders, incident commanders, SRE owners, legal/compliance liaisons, and customer success.

Scope

- Applies to all production incidents impacting API availability, latency SLOs, and data integrity for hosted and dedicated customers.
- Does NOT replace customer-specific contractual obligations (see related contract folder).

Quick summary of responsibilities

- Incident Commander (IC): decides to invoke forensic evidence collection and SLA-credit evaluation.
- Primary responder / SRE: collects evidence per the runbook below.
- Service owner: prepares the SLA credit recommendation and customer remediation plan.
- Legal/Compliance: sign-off when evidence contains PII or long-term retention is requested.
- Customer Success (CS): coordinates customer comms and credit issuance.

Definitions and severity mapping (for this playbook)

1) Sev 0 / P0: Complete service outage for > 5 minutes affecting > 30% of traffic for a single region or tenant-impacting outage for a paid customer.
2) Sev 1 / P1: Major degradation of latency SLO with measurable error escalation, or sustained SLO misses > 5 minutes.
3) Sev 2 / P2: Partial degradations, single-tenant performance issues limited to a small subset of requests.

Evidence retention windows (default internal policy)

- Aggregated metrics (Prometheus/Long-term metrics): 7 years (rollup retention).
- High-resolution metrics (1s/5s scrape): 90 days.
- Traces (Jaeger/OTel): 180 days.
- API request/response logs (structured): 90 days, except customer-flagged incidents where hold extends to 2 years on legal approval.
- Raw request payloads / model inputs & outputs: 30 days by default; extended hold requires legal approval and customer consent.
- KV-cache snapshots and model internal state dumps: stored on a per-incident S3 folder for 365 days when retained for RCA.
- Core dumps and GPU telemetry: 365 days when collected.

Retention exceptions and legal hold

- To place evidence on legal hold, IC must request Legal via the incident bridge with a documented justification. Legal will respond in 24 hours and create a long-term evidence artifact entry in the Evidence Ledger.
- Customer requests for data to be kept or revoked must be forwarded to Legal + CS and handled per the Data Residency policy.

Evidence collection runbook (sequence to run during/after containment)

1) Triage & snapshot (first 10 minutes once IC grants collection):
   - Note time window: record UTC start/end timestamps for evidence scope (e.g., 2025-02-12T15:42:00Z -> 2025-02-12T16:12:00Z).
   - Create S3 incident folder: s3://redwood-incident-evidence/{incident-id}/ (IC or primary responder creates).
   - Take an etcd/config snapshot of feature flags and routing rules and upload: 
     - CLI: etcdctl snapshot save /tmp/{incident-id}-etcd.db && aws s3 cp /tmp/{incident-id}-etcd.db s3://redwood-incident-evidence/{incident-id}/config/
   - Lock deployment state: annotate the release manifest and record sha/tag.

2) Logs and structured request capture (10-30 minutes):
   - Export API logs for affected time window:
     - Example: aws logs start-query --log-group-name "/redwood/apigw" --start-time 1707750000 --end-time 1707753600 --query-string 'fields @timestamp, @message | filter tenantId = "T-123" or level = "ERROR"'
   - Capture nginx/proxy configs and last 50k lines: sudo journalctl -u nginx -n 50000 > /tmp/nginx-tail.log
   - Persist request/response payloads if needed: use the forensic exporter script: /opt/infra/bin/forensic-export --start 2025-02-12T15:42:00Z --end 2025-02-12T16:12:00Z --tenant T-123 --out s3://redwood-incident-evidence/{incident-id}/requests.jsonl

3) Traces and spans (10-60 minutes):
   - Query Jaeger/OTel for the window and affected services:
     - curl -G "https://jaeger.internal/api/traces?service=inference-gateway&start=1707750000&end=1707753600" > /tmp/traces.json
   - Include sampled spans and annotate with mapping to API log IDs.

4) Model-level artifacts (when model quality or outputs are suspect):
   - Save model inputs/outputs snapshot (obfuscate PII by default): python scripts/save_model_io.py --incident {incident-id} --tenant T-123 --mask-pii true --out s3://redwood-incident-evidence/{incident-id}/model-io/
   - Save KV-cache dump if relevant: /opt/runtime/bin/dump-kv-cache --pid <serving-pid> --out /tmp/kv-{incident-id}.bin && aws s3 cp /tmp/kv-{incident-id}.bin s3://redwood-incident-evidence/{incident-id}/runtime/

5) Low-level telemetry and hardware diagnostics (when GPU failures suspected):
   - nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,name,utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu,memory.used --format=csv -l 1 > /tmp/gpu-{incident-id}.csv
   - Collect dmesg, kernel logs and systemd journal for the time window.

6) Put everything in S3 and record a manifest:
   - Example manifest format (single-line JSON per artifact in manifest file): {"artifact":"requests.jsonl","path":"s3://...","sha256":"<hash>","retention":"90d"}
   - Save manifest as s3://redwood-incident-evidence/{incident-id}/MANIFEST.jsonl and add evidence ledger entry.

Evidence handling safeguards

- Masking: default to PII masking on model I/O snapshots unless IC/Legal explicitly requests raw retention.
- Access: evidence S3 prefixes are ACL'd; only members of the Incident Evidence group (IAM role: incident-evidence) + Legal can access by default.
- Audit: all downloads must be logged and added to the MANIFEST.

SLA credit determination and calculation

When to consider an SLA credit

- A Sev0 outage that causes the customer to miss the monthly availability SLO (monthly availability < contracted threshold) is eligible.
- Sustained latency SLO miss that exceeds contractual penalty window (per-customer SLA language).
- Service degradations where root cause matches causation in contract (e.g., platform capacity vs. customer misconfiguration).

Credit calculation (standard example)

- Contract: 99.9% monthly availability target.
- Measured availability for the contract month: 99.55% (total downtime = 130 minutes).
- Monthly credit formula: credit = min(30%, (downtime_minutes / total_minutes_in_month) * 100 * multiplier)
  - Example multiplier = 1 for single region outage.
  - total_minutes_in_month = 30 * 24 * 60 = 43,200.
  - credit = min(30%, (130 / 43,200) * 100) = min(30%, 0.301%) = 0.301% of monthly bill credited.

Operational checklist to recommend a credit

- Confirm incident timeline and affected tenant(s) with evidence manifest.
- Confirm SLO exposed to customer and compute measured violation window.
- Determine root cause category and whether platform is at fault.
- Prepare credit calculation and deduction against the invoice.
- Legal/Finance sign-off for credits > 5% of monthly invoice.

Customer comms templates (short, fill-in placeholders)

1) Initial acknowledgement (within 1 hour):

Subject: Redwood Incident #{incident-id} — Acknowledgement

Hello {customer_name},

We detected an impact to {service_name} affecting {scope/tenants}. Our on-call team is actively investigating. We will provide a status update within 60 minutes.

If you have urgent information to share, reply to this message or contact your CS rep, {cs_rep}.

Regards,
Redwood Incident Response Team

2) Status update (30–60 minute cadence while active):

Subject: Redwood Incident #{incident-id} — Status update

Summary: {short summary}
Impact: {tenant list / percentage of request rate affected}
Mitigation in progress: {actions being taken}
Next update: {time}

3) Post-incident summary & credits (post RCA):

Subject: Redwood Incident #{incident-id} — Post-incident summary and next steps

Summary of impact: {detailed timeline}
Root cause: {root cause description}
Actions taken: {mitigation and long-term fixes}
SLA impact & credit calculation: {credit % / amount} (see attached computation)
Action items and owners: {task list}

We apologize for the disruption. Your CS lead {cs_rep} will follow up to coordinate crediting and next steps.

Postmortem & SLA evidence pack requirements

For all Sev0 and Sev1 incidents the postmortem must include:
- Title, date, incident lead, author and list of reviewers.
- Executive summary (1–3 sentences).
- Impact and timeline with UTC timestamps.
- Evidence manifest and S3 links to collected artifacts with retention flags.
- Root cause analysis with contributing factors.
- Action item list with owner, priority, ETA and verification method.
- SLA calculation spreadsheet or exported computation and formula used.
- Attach customer communication history (initial ack, status updates, final notes).

Timeline for documentation

- Sev0: IC must publish an initial timeline stub within 24 hours. Full postmortem draft (including evidence manifest and credit recommendation) within 7 business days. Finalized postmortem after reviewer sign-off within 14 business days.
- Sev1: Postmortem draft within 10 business days, final within 21 business days.

On-call succession & handover checklist (succession play)

When handing off to the next rotation or promoting a responder to IC, ensure the following checklist is completed:
- Confirm incident bridge is healthy and pinned contact list is accurate.
- Share the incident timeline and attach MANIFEST link.
- Confirm any ongoing evidence collection jobs (script PIDs, S3 upload in progress).
- Mark any customer comms that are pending with deadlines.
- Confirm that the new IC has access to incident-evidence role.
- If long-term retention needed, confirm Legal has been paged.

Game day checklist (pre-run verification for evidence readiness)

- Verify incident-evidence IAM role exists for test responders and contains no live-customer access.
- Simulate a capture: run /opt/infra/bin/forensic-export against synthetic tenant and ensure artifacts land in the test S3 prefix and are listed in a MANIFEST.
- Run end-to-end upload and retrieval test for traces (Jaeger) -> S3 export -> MANIFEST integrity check.
- Verify PII masking pipeline triggers and sample masked artifacts.
- Confirm automation can extend retention on a manifest entry with a Legal approval token.

Operational guardrails and SLO protection patterns

- Prefer mitigations that reduce blast radius (regional failover, model-variant routing) before mass collection of raw payloads.
- Collection of raw model inputs/outputs requires explicit IC justification to balance privacy risk.

Appendix A: Example PromQL snippets for evidence

- 99th percentile latency for inference-gateway in time window:
  - histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
- Error-rate for tenant T-123:
  - sum(rate(inference_requests_total{tenant_id="T-123",status!~"2.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(inference_requests_total{tenant_id="T-123"}[5m]))

Appendix B: Evidence MANIFEST example (one line per artifact)

- {"artifact":"nginx-tail.log","path":"s3://redwood-incident-evidence/{incident-id}/logs/nginx-tail.log","sha256":"<hash>","retention":"90d"}
- {"artifact":"model-io/requests.jsonl","path":"s3://redwood-incident-evidence/{incident-id}/model-io/requests.jsonl","sha256":"<hash>","retention":"30d"}

Appendix C: Escalation contact quick list

- IC: incident@redwood.internal (primary bridge)
- On-call infra lead: oncall-infra@redwood.internal
- Legal: legal@redwood.internal (24-hour response)
- CS escalation: cs-esc@redwood.internal

Document maintenance

- Owner: engineering (oncall program). Review cadence: quarterly.
- This document should be exercised during at least two game days per calendar year and after any major platform release that affects request routing or data capture paths.

End of playbook
